A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIMS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial changes to the framework and evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original SIMS simulation results, motion-diversity measurements, policy ablations, script-execution experiments, and a 12-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulation results, planning and dataset ablations, unseen-object evaluations, a 30-participant user study, and newly captured ViconStyle data.

M1.justification: V1's video/VLM/audio extraction and graph-edit-distance scene selection are replaced by prompted short-script construction and style-filtered CLIP retrieval followed by LLM composition for a supplied scene. V2 also adds Idle and Carry policies and replaces the 15-joint contact representation with locomotion, human-scene interaction, and dynamic-object goal/reward templates. These are procedural changes beyond renaming the controller.

E1.justification: V2 adds COUCH, AMASS, and the captured ViconStyle dataset alongside retained SAMP, 100Style, and CIRCLE data. Evaluated capabilities expand to Idle and dynamic-object carrying. The explicitly identified ScanNet evaluation and simple/mid/hard script-execution scenarios reported in v1 are no longer reported.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 includes NSM, SAMP, AMP, and AMP(VC), which disappear from the numerical baseline comparison in v2 Table 3; InterPhys, InterScene, and UniHSI remain. V2 Table 4 adds re-implemented InterPhys to the motion-diversity comparison for Carry. V2's separate capability matrix does not restore the removed experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Furniture training changes from a half-training/half-testing split of 80 PartNet objects to 3DFront furniture. The user study changes from 12 to 30 participants, revises its comparison controls, and replaces script alignment with motion diversity, plot engagement, and emotional resonance ratings. A new planning protocol evaluates 200 samples per method using approximately 20 keyframes, SBERT similarity, and generation time.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative direct-generation versus retrieval ablation, cross-dataset unseen-object testing, and training-data ablations for Walk, Carry, Sit, and Lie (Tables 6–10). The retained heightmap/text ablation adds APD and Carry while dropping Reach. V1's difficulty-dependent execution analysis and detailed comparative narrative case studies are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report motion-diversity evaluation with 1024 sequences aggregated over 10 trials and APD values with plus/minus uncertainty. V2 extends this reporting format to additional results without documenting a changed repetition count, seed policy, uncertainty estimator, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Reported SIMS Sit/Lie success changes from 90.0/79.2 in v1 Table 1 to 98.1/87.6 in v2 Table 3 under changed training settings, so these are not controlled performance gains. Lie FID changes from 164.88 to 171.24. V2 adds Carry, planning, generalization, and dataset-ablation results, replaces user-study scores, and removes the earlier difficulty-stratified execution results.

T1.justification: Appendix reward definitions change substantively: contact reward weights move from 0.6/0.4 to 0.7/0.3, the near/far terms are revised, and new dynamic-object rewards are defined. These are localized mathematical changes. The MotionCLIP reconstruction/alignment equations are retained and relocated; no theorem or proof contribution is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions shift from real-video-grounded script planning and scene-graph retrieval to retrieval-augmented script generation, modular skill extensibility, and broader stylized control supported by newly captured data. The overarching claim of long-term, physically plausible, stylized human-scene interaction remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations attributing improved walking stability to AMASS and richer interaction styles to COUCH/ViconStyle. V1's explicit connection between data scarcity and limited generalization, its temporal-coherence limitation, and its explanation of deficient pose transitions are removed. More data collection remains future work, alongside new finger-articulation and multi-agent directions.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies a 12×12 heightmap with 0.15-meter spacing and documents ViconStyle capture, fitting, annotation, and object reconstruction, including 120 fps, three actors, 415 clips, and 71.6 minutes. A project-page link replaces the future code/data-release promise, although the PDFs do not establish downloadable availability. Most MotionCLIP implementation details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V2 introduces systematic positioning against seven HSI methods through automation, style control, scalability, and skill coverage (Table 1). It adds references supporting RAG, SBERT, captured data, and newer controllers such as CALM and MaskedMimic, while removing HumanVLA, PlaMo, and references supporting the discarded video/audio and graph-matching pipeline.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Method and experiment sections are reorganized, the language-conditioned-control survey is replaced by comparative positioning, MotionCLIP details move into the supplement, and the lengthy narrative appendix is substantially condensed and restructured.

P2.justification: The teaser, pipeline, narrative demonstrations, and qualitative skill figures are substantially redesigned. V2 adds a capability matrix, dataset and ablation tables, and capture/scalability figures, while removing the video-extraction illustration and lengthy comparative script tables. Part of the earlier controller diagram is reused in the appendix rather than being wholly new.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical grounding and reproducibility through the 200-sample planning comparison, training-data ablations, unseen-object testing, and documented ViconStyle capture. These benefits are partly offset by removal of v1's long-horizon difficulty results, several numerical baselines, and explicit limitations. Changed experimental settings also prevent interpreting the higher contact-success scores as controlled gains, making the net quality improvement limited.
